conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced was found. The main item is arithmetic in Abbott's own releases: the 6.5-7.5% FY comparable-sales guide, after H1 at 3.7% and 4.8%, needs about 8.5-10.5% in H2, while the ~$13.0B revenue consensus implies only ~7% in Q3, so a trim to the FY sales guide is likely and largely expected. Small proxy positives (nutrition sequential momentum, August COVID wave, depressed positioning) offset it. abs_move 6.0 sits on the 5.5% implied move and the 6.0% median reaction, nudged up because the FY guide is likely to move. p_up 48 is a faint lean, so the scaled number is close to zero. impact_sum -0.2 and impact_scaled -0.24 agree.
bar: Q3 adj EPS: company guide $1.38-1.46 (Q2 release https://abbott.mediaroom.com/2026-07-16-Abbott-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-EPS-Guidance); consensus ~$1.42, from Zacks/Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/abt) and Benzinga, which agree. Q3 revenue consensus $12,995M (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/abbott-q3-2026-earnings-preview-abt-revenue-guidance-key-drivers, 2026-10-05), and other previews say $12.9-13.0B. FY26 guide: comparable sales +6.5-7.5%, adj EPS $5.45-5.60.
positioning_check: Short interest 22.6M shares, 1.30% of float, 1.7 days to cover, settlement around 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/ABT), so not crowded. Skew_25d is +0.93 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.24, ATM spread 21% of mid. The stock is 20.9% below its 52-week high, was oversold at $98.83 (RSI 29) on 2026-09-30 (https://www.money365.market/news/latest/abbott-shares-decline-2-10-as-industry-report-forecasts-sensor-87666ad7), and is $103.24 now (+4.5% in October, 20d -0.43%). Sentiment is depressed but no squeeze setup exists.

findings.finding: Abbott's own figures (Q1 comparable +3.7%, Q2 +4.8%, FY guide reaffirmed at +6.5-7.5% comparable including Exact) need about +8.5% (low end) to +10.5% (high end) comparable growth in H2. The $12,995M Q3 revenue consensus, against a pro-forma Q3-25 base of about $12.24B ($11,393M Abbott + $851M Exact) and the company's ~-1% Q3 FX, implies only about +7% comparable. The street already models below the guide path, and a trim of the FY sales range to ~6% (EPS held) is the likely outcome on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moves have driven this name's reactions: Apr-2026 EPS guide cut (Exact dilution, weak flu) -6.0%; Jan-2026 weak Q4 plus soft outlook -10.0%; Jul-2026 EPS raise with sales guide reaffirmed +10.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus revenue already sits below the guide-implied path, and the stock fell about 6% from the post-Q2 level (~$110) to $103. If a trim were fully priced, the street would sit at or below the low end in public and the skew would not be flat. A trim is expected, but its size and whether EPS is held are open.
findings.independence: Q1 comparable +3.7% is from the Q1 release (https://abbott.mediaroom.com/2026-04-16-Abbott-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results-Updates-Guidance-to-Reflect-Acquisition-of-Exact-Sciences). The consensus is from Hudson Labs (separate source). Exact Q3-25 revenue of $851M is from the Exact 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1124140/000112414025000090/exas-20251103xex991.htm). The arithmetic is mine.

findings.finding: The Q3 adj EPS bar ($1.42 consensus) sits exactly mid-guide ($1.38-1.46). Abbott beat by $0.03 in Q2 ($1.31 vs ~$1.28) and the Q2 mix carried adjusted gross margin up 100bp to 58.0%, so a $0.01-0.03 beat inside the guided range is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Small EPS beats inside the guide have not moved this stock on their own: Oct-2025 in-line EPS -2.9%, Apr-2025 +2.8%, Jan-2025 +0.9%. The large moves came from sales and guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The beat lands inside what the company guided, and Abbott habitually lands slightly above the midpoint, so the street expects it.
findings.independence: The Q2 beat size is from finviz (https://finviz.com/news/369103/abbott-raises-2026-earnings-outlook-after-second-quarter-results-beat-expectations-abt).

findings.finding: Nutrition (~17% of sales) needs only about +$67M sequential to hit the street's ~+2.7% YoY on the $2,153M Q3-25 base. Q2 nutrition already rose $127M sequentially to $2,144M, international pediatric grew +6.4%, and management called Q3 the 'cleanest' nutrition quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nutrition misses drove the Jan-2026 -10.0% (volume loss after late-2025 price actions) and fed into Apr-2026 -6.0%. A return to growth was part of the Jul-2026 +10.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly. The street models a return to growth (Zacks ~+2.7%), but the sequential run-rate implies the bar is low. If that were priced, nutrition would not appear as the top risk in previews (Hudson Labs lists 'nutrition volume response unproven'). Net of the rest of the company: nutrition beating by 2pts is worth only ~0.3pt of total growth, against a ~9% H2 need.
findings.independence: Hudson Labs preview, 2026-10-05: Q3-25 nutrition base $2,153M; the Zacks estimate is via search. Nestlé had an infant-formula recall in Q1 2026 (https://www.foodnavigator-usa.com/Article/2026/04/23/nestle-q1-2026-sales-rise-as-coffee-and-confectionery-offset-infant-formula-recall/), a proxy for international share. Same primary document as finding 1.

findings.finding: A US summer COVID wave built through August 2026: CDC test positivity rose from 3.1% (week to Aug 1) to 4.8% (week to Aug 15), with cases growing in all 50 states. That supports Rapid Diagnostics after Q2 rapid/molecular fell -8.0% (US -14.5%) on a weak respiratory season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A weak respiratory season was named in the Apr-2026 guide cut (-6.0%). COVID testing is now small, so upside is limited.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission that Abbott has not confirmed, and Q3-25 also had a summer wave, so the YoY lift is uncertain. If it were priced, previews would flag rapid diagnostics as an upside item. They do not mention it.
findings.independence: NBC summer-wave coverage, Aug 2026 (https://www.nbcpalmsprings.com/your-health-today/2026/08/20/covid-cases-are-rising-across-the-us-as-summer-wave-builds). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: J&J (reported 2026-10-13, after Abbott last spoke) grew MedTech only +2.5% operationally. Its call put electrophysiology at about +4.4%, with pulsed-field-ablation competition sharper in Asia-Pacific. A share donor in EP is consistent with Abbott's guided EP acceleration (Q2 EP +13.4%, Volt/TactiFlex Duo), but the share may be flowing to Boston Scientific instead.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EP is one of the four lines carrying ~80% of the guided H2 acceleration. There is no isolated reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer read with an ambiguous sign: J&J losing EP share does not identify who gains. The EP growth figure is from a call summary, not the release.
findings.independence: Call summary via https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/johnson-johnson-q3-2026-earnings-rise-medtech-lags. It is the same company event as the source, so not independent.

findings.finding: Competition for Cologuard (Exact, ~$919M a quarter, Q2 comparable +13.3%, H2 guided to mid-teens) is building. Guardant's Shield blood test ran ~66,000 tests in Q2 2026 (vs ~16,000 a year earlier), Guardant raised its FY Shield guide to 270-285k tests, and UnitedHealthcare added first-line coverage after the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior Abbott print with Exact in the base. Cancer diagnostics is one of the four named H2 accelerators.
findings.why_not_priced: Shield volume is small next to Cologuard's (roughly 70k vs over 1M tests a quarter), and Abbott also sells a blood test (Freenome). If this were priced, previews would treat mid-teens H2 as at risk. They list it as a driver.
findings.independence: none (a single Guardant-derived source). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 (8-K items 7.01/8.01) Abbott agreed to pay about $670M to resolve the Gill NEC verdict plus claims for ~2,000 infants. The cost will appear as a Q3 GAAP specified item, excluded from adjusted EPS. About 1,700 suits covering 12,700 infants remain. The $385M DOJ formula settlement (announced Sept 2026) was already reserved in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no print reaction tied to litigation charges. They sit below the adjusted line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: public for two months and excluded from adjusted EPS. It is filed so a judge sees the GAAP gap ($1.01 GAAP consensus vs $1.42 adjusted) is explained.
findings.independence: Bloomberg Government (https://news.bgov.com/litigation/abbott-will-pay-670-million-to-end-2-000-infant-formula-claims). Q2 release: $385M legal reserve.

findings.finding: FY2027 EPS estimates sit near $6.05 (e.g., Erste $6.06, 2026-07-29), about +9.5% over the FY26 guide midpoint of $5.525. That is high-single-digit growth with Exact dilution still in the base and nutrition only recovering. Abbott has given next-year color on past Q3 calls, so any early 2027 framing below ~$6 is a risk inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Outlook-driven reactions are the large ones for this name (-10.0% Jan-2026, -6.0% Apr-2026).
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference. Whether Abbott comments on 2027 at all is unknown, and the long-term target of high-single-digit to double-digit EPS growth (Q2 call) is consistent with consensus. If the market doubted the 2027 number, ABT would trade below ~17x a $6 figure. At $103 it is ~17x, so mild doubt is already in the price.
findings.independence: Barchart's July preview also puts FY27 at $6.05 (via search). The long-term target is from the Q2 call summary (vectorshift).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is light and negative-leaning without being a crowded short. The stock is 21% off its high and fell to an oversold $98.83 on 2026-09-30, with short interest only 1.3% of float (1.7 days) and a flat skew (+0.93). The last print with depressed sentiment and a reaffirmed sales guide (Jul-2026) paid +10.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul-2026 +10.7% came from a similar low-expectation setup; Jan-2026 -10.0% came from a similar setup on a miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself. The asymmetry is that a sales-guide trim the street already models below may be absorbed, as in July. But the stock is already +4.5% off the September low, so some of that is spent.
findings.independence: Short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/ABT. Skew: sealed baseline.

outside_window.finding: Medicare national competitive bidding for CGMs/insulin pumps (finalised Nov 2025) takes effect no earlier than 2028-01-01. Any Libre pricing hit lies far beyond this window.
Dexcom's Q3 2026 print, the direct CGM read-across, comes after Abbott's window. Dexcom Q2 (2026-07-30) grew +13%, with Abbott Libre the main competitor.

baseline_tension: Consistent with the baseline. The skew is flat and the run-up near zero, and the evidence is balanced: an expected FY sales-guide trim against low positioning and modest segment tailwinds. Nothing found argues against the option market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guided range is expected): the EPS-beat finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2, since $1.42 sits mid-guide
Lesson 9 (size a segment net of the rest): the nutrition finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because nutrition is ~17% of sales and the H2 need is company-wide
Lesson 1/2: the guidance finding kept at -0.8 because this name's reactions turn on guidance, not on the EPS line; the one-off settlement kept at 0
